land.text: Fars: 'Ali ibn Buya (Imad al-Dawla) in 934 conquered Fars and made Shiraz his capital'

predecessors.note: Infobox: preceded by the Abbasid Caliphate, the Ziyarids, the Banu Ilyas and Abu Abdallah al-Baridi. Isfahan and Khuzestan (935, from the Ziyarid side), Ray (943) and Baghdad (945) came later and are ledger gains; the caliphs stayed in Baghdad under Buyid control, which Cliopatria draws as 'Abbasid Caliphate/Buyid Dynasty' 947-969.

land.text: Fars, the last Buyid seat, to 1062

successors.note: Infobox: disestablished 1062; the page names the Seljuk Empire among the successors but not the conqueror of Fars. Baghdad went to Tughril in 1055; Ray to the Ghaznavids in 1029; Isfahan and Hamadan to the Kakuyids; Mosul to the Uqaylids (989): those are ledger events, not the handover at the end.

capitals.name: Shiraz
capitals.note: Infobox 'Shiraz (Buyids of Fars, 934-1062)'. The Buyids had three seats at once; Adud al-Dawla's court was 'Shiraz, with frequent visits to Baghdad' (Adud page).

rulers.name: Imad al-Dawla (Ali ibn Buya)
rulers.title: amir of Fars
rulers.note: Fars line, the one that spans the whole life of the state; the Jibal line (Rukn al-Dawla 935-976, Fakhr al-Dawla, Majd al-Dawla to 1029) and the Iraq line (Mu'izz al-Dawla 945-967, 'Izz al-Dawla, Adud al-Dawla 978-983, ... Al-Malik al-Rahim 1048-1055) are in the notes.

rulers.name: Adud al-Dawla (Fanna Khusraw)
rulers.title: amir of Fars
rulers.note: Succeeded in Fars when 'Imad al-Dawla died in December 949' (Adud page); died at Baghdad on 26 March 983; Iraq from 978.

rulers.name: Abu Mansur Fulad Sutun (restored)
rulers.title: amir of Fars
rulers.note: The page prints '1051-1062' for this reign, which overlaps Khusrau Shah's 1051-1054; the restored reign is started in 1054 here.

correction.text: Fars, Khuzestan, Jibal and Iraq under the three Buyid brothers; the caliph at Baghdad was their figurehead (not a page of this dossier)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 947-969, replacing Cliopatria's gap: the Buyid Dynasty row has no shape for these 23 years, and the row 'Abbasid Caliphate/Buyid Dynasty' (947-969, 735,812 km2; Wikipedia 'Abbasid Caliphate', SeshatID ir_buyid_confederation, the Buyid's own) draws Fars, Khuzestan, Hamadan, Baghdad and Basra under the same Wikidata id as the Abbasids. The page puts the Buyids at Shiraz, Ray and Baghdad throughout, so this is the Buyid state; Kerman is added by the 967 gain. The Abbasid Caliphate's own dossier may use the same row.

1.08 M km2 for 970-979, against the infobox's 1.6 M km2 'est. 980' (ratio 0.67 to the 980 shape's 1.31 M: 0.82): Fars, Khuzestan, Isfahan, Kerman (Adud 'conquered all of Kerman' in 967), Iraq with Baghdad, a coastal strip of Oman (largely conquered by 972, including Sohar, on the Adud page). Left alone: the Jibal dynastic splits are internal.

1.31 M km2 for 980-989 against the infobox's 1.6 M km2 'est. 980' (ratio 0.82). Matches the page: the Jazira with Mosul (979), Tabaristan (980) and Gorgan (981) added to the 970 shape; 'The Buyid dynasty reached its zenith under Fanna Khusraw (r. 949-983)'. Gorgan covers only 16% of its cells here, as Gurgan fell in 981.

1.13 M km2 for 990-999. The Jazira is gone as the Uqaylids occupied 'Mosul and the Diyar Rabi'a ... in 989' (the infobox founding is 990), matching the shape. But Tabaristan and Gurgan stay in it to 999 although 'After Fakhr al-Dawla's death in 997, the Ziyarid Qabus conquered Tabaristan and Gurgan' (Majd al-Dawla page): valid 990-996, and the next keyframe covers 997-999.

correction.text: Fars, the last Buyid ground (Fulad Sutun, to 1062)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1056-1062: after Baghdad fell in 1055 the Buyid line survived in Fars until 'Disestablished: 1062' (infobox). Cliopatria's row ends in 1055.

ledger.note: 934: Ali ibn Buya (Imad al-Dawla) conquers Fars and makes Shiraz his capital. The page: 'in 934 conquered Fars and made Shiraz his capital'; infobox 'Established: 934'. Cliopatria starts the row in 936.

935: Khuzestan falls to the Buyids. The page's table: 'After Mardavij's assassination, Ali and Ahmad conquer Khuzistan'. The previous owner is not named; the Ziyarid link is my reading (Mardavij was the Ziyarid ruler) and the infobox also lists Abu Abdallah al-Baridi among the predecessors.
935: Isfahan, 'the Ziyarid capital', is taken after Mardavij's assassination; the sources say Hasan ibn Buya captured it.

ledger.counterpart: unnamed rulers of the Jibal (page silent)
ledger.note: 943: Hasan ibn Buya (Rukn al-Dawla) takes Ray and makes it his capital. 'By 943 managed to capture Ray, which he made his capital'; parts of Jibal fell in the late 930s. The previous holders are not named by the page.

945: Ahmad ibn Buya (Mu'izz al-Dawla) takes Baghdad. 'In 945, the youngest brother, Ahmad ibn Buya, conquered Iraq and made Baghdad his capital'; 'In 945, Ahmad entered Iraq and seized control of Baghdad'. The page gives no month.

967: Kerman is conquered. 'Adud al-Dawla conquered all of Kerman, and appointed his son Shirdil Abu'l-Fawaris as the viceroy of the province', taking advantage of a quarrel among the Ilyasids; the Buyid page: 'Kerman was conquered in 967'.

972: Oman is largely conquered. 'A campaign began in 966 with Mu'izz al-Dawla. Oman was largely conquered in 972, including Sohar.' The Buyid page's table says 'Oman (967)'. Cliopatria's Buyid shapes hold only a coastal strip of Oman.

region.text: Mosul, Diyar Bakr and Diyar Mudar

ledger.note: 978: Adud al-Dawla marches on Mosul. 'On 29 May 978, Izz al-Dawla, along with Abu Taghlib, invaded the domains of Adud al-Dawla' and was defeated, captured and executed; 'After the 978 victory he marched on Mosul and captured it' and stayed a year, during which his army 'conquered Diyar Bakr and Diyar Mudar'. The Hamdanids briefly retook Mayyafariqin.
979: the Jazira passes to the Buyids. The page's table: 'the Jazira (979)'; the Uqaylid page: the Buwayhids 'had expelled the Hamdanids from Mosul in 979'.

region.text: Mosul, Diyar Bakr and Diyar Mudar

ledger.note: 979: the Hamdanids are driven off. Adud 'then spent a year there' after the 978 victory; the Hamdanids' brief return to Mayyafariqin is the last fighting the page gives.
980: Tabaristan is conquered. The page's table: 'Tabaristan (980), and Gorgan (981)'; the Adud page has him help his brother Mu'ayyad al-Dawla take Tabaristan and Gurgan from Qabus in late 980.
981: Gurgan is conquered, from the Ziyarid Qabus: 'Gorgan (981)'.

989: Mosul and the Diyar Rabi'a pass to the Uqaylids. 'Mosul and the Diyar Rabi'a was occupied in 989' (the infobox founding is 990). The year is the page's; that the land came from the Buyids is my reading (they held Mosul from 979). In 996 al-Muqallad forced 'its Buwayhid governor to flee', and a treaty then made him 'nominally subservient to the Buwayhids' (undated). Cliopatria drops the Jazira in 990.
997: Qabus retakes Tabaristan and Gurgan. 'After Fakhr al-Dawla's death in 997, the Ziyarid Qabus conquered Tabaristan and Gurgan'; Majd al-Dawla failed to repel him.

region.text: Isfahan and Hamadan under Ala al-Dawla Muhammad

ledger.note: 1023: Ala al-Dawla becomes a nominal vassal. He captured Hamadan in 1023, ending Sama' al-Dawla's rule (r. 1021-1023), and after 1023 was 'virtually an independent monarch' who still minted coins in Majd al-Dawla's name; his rule at Isfahan dated from at least 1003 ('the start of the Kakuyid dynasty'). [Reviewer me-08-c, 2026-10-19: confidence 2: the Majd al-Dawla page dates the capture of Hamadan to 1023 but gives no date for Isfahan's autonomy.]
1029: the Kakuyid coinage in Majd al-Dawla's name ends. Ala al-Dawla 'kept minting coins in Majd al-Dawla's name until 1029'.

1029: Mahmud of Ghazni takes Ray. 'Mahmud conquered Ray in March/April 1029', deposing Majd al-Dawla, who was 'reportedly sent to the Ghaznavid capital'; his pretext was Majd's request for help against his Daylamite soldiers.

1041: Kerman passes to the Seljuk Qavurt. The Qavurt page: he 'defeated the Buyid ruler's army in Kerman and Makran in around 1041 CE' and 'brought Kerman under his control, some of his attacks were repelled by Kalijar around 1042'. The Buyid page lists Qawam al-Dawla in Kerman 1012-1028; Kerman then stayed with Abu Kalijar. [Reviewer me-08-c, 2026-10-19: was 1028, confidence 1, the date of Cliopatria's shape; corrected from the Qavurt page.]

1055: Tughril takes Baghdad. 'In 1055, Tughril conquered Baghdad, the seat of the caliphate, and ousted the last of the Buyid rulers.' The Tughril page gives the entry as 'the 25th of Ramadan, 447 AH' and has Malik al-Rahim taken prisoner at the end of Ramadan.

1062: the Buyid line of Fars ends. Infobox 'Disestablished: 1062'; the Fars list ends with Abu Mansur Fulad Sutun (1051-1062). The page does not name who took Shiraz; the Seljuk Empire is on the successor list.

wars.name: Buyid conquest of Baghdad
wars.outcome: Ahmad ibn Buya 'entered Iraq and seized control of Baghdad' in 945 and made it his capital.

wars.name: Buyid civil war of 974-978
wars.outcome: Adud al-Dawla beat Izz al-Dawla at Ahvaz (1 July 977) and at Samarra (29 May 978, Izz al-Dawla having come with the Hamdanid Abu Taghlib), had him executed and held Iraq; in 974-975 he had earlier forced him to abdicate (12 March 975) before Rukn al-Dawla restored him.
wars.note: A fight inside the dynasty; no territory left Buyid hands.

wars.name: Buyid-Hamdanid war for Mosul and the Jazira
wars.outcome: Adud al-Dawla took Mosul after the 978 victory, spent a year there and conquered Diyar Bakr and Diyar Mudar; the Hamdanids briefly retook Mayyafariqin, Abu Taghlib fled to Rahba; the Jazira is dated 979.

wars.name: Buyid conquest of Tabaristan and Gurgan
wars.outcome: Mu'ayyad al-Dawla, helped by Adud al-Dawla, took Tabaristan and Gurgan from Qabus in late 980; Gorgan is dated 981. Qabus retook both after 997.

wars.name: Buyid-Samanid and Saffarid frontier
wars.outcome: Peace without a border change: in 968 Khalaf ibn Ahmad 'recognized Buyid authority'; in 972 Adud al-Dawla and Rukn al-Dawla paid the Samanids 150,000 dinars after the Baloch campaign that ended on 8 January 972.
wars.note: The pages give no dated Samanid campaigns in Khorasan; 'the borders of Khorasan in the east' is the frontier. The Saffarid recognition is not written as a vassal event because the page gives no end.

wars.name: Uqaylid occupation of Mosul
wars.outcome: The Uqaylids occupied Mosul and the Diyar Rabi'a in 989, forced the Buwayhid governor to flee in 996 and then agreed a treaty that made al-Muqallad 'nominally subservient to the Buwayhids, but in effect he was independent'.

wars.name: Ghaznavid conquest of Ray
wars.outcome: Mahmud conquered Ray in March/April 1029 and deposed Majd al-Dawla; Fana-Khusrau failed to restore Buyid power.

wars.name: Seljuk conquest of Baghdad
wars.outcome: Tughril entered Baghdad in 1055 (25 Ramadan 447 AH) and took Malik al-Rahim prisoner; the Buyids of Fars survived to 1062.
wars.note: Arslan al-Basasiri entered Baghdad for the Fatimids in 1059 (the page; the Uqaylid page says the end of 1058), a Fatimid-claimed Baghdad outside this dossier's life.

certainty.note: Frontiers are approximate throughout: the dynasty was a confederation of three amirates whose borders with the Samanids ('the borders of Khorasan'), Hamdanids and Byzantines (the Syrian front) are not fixed by any treaty on the pages opened.

notes: Row question (data/README, owned table): Cliopatria carries Wikidata Q12536 (the Abbasid Caliphate's item) on the Buyid Dynasty, Abbasid Caliphate and Abbasid Caliphate/Buyid Dynasty rows. The Buyids are a different state from the caliphate (their own capitals, rulers and 934 founding on the page), so this dossier keeps only the Name 'Buyid Dynasty' in cliopatria_names and keeps Q12536 in identity only because the schema asks for Cliopatria's value; it looks wrong for the Buyids and the Wikidata owner should check. The 947-969 row 'Abbasid Caliphate/Buyid Dynasty' (SeshatID ir_buyid_confederation, the same as the Buyid row) is the Buyid state in the years Cliopatria's Buyid row lacks; this dossier adopts its shape as the new keyframe buyid-dynasty_947 without taking the Name into cliopatria_names, so the abbasid-caliphate-buyid-dynasty dossier (another part of me-08) may also draw it; the renderer should draw it once. Cliopatria's Buyid shapes drop Fars from 1028 although the page keeps the Buyids at Shiraz to 1062; the correction adds Fars back (admin1 Fars, 'Iran') and a keyframe covers 1056-1062. Isfahan and Hamadan are written as a vassal span 1023-1029 (the Kakuyids), not as a loss. Unverified within the 5-page budget: when Kerman, Khuzestan (Taj al-Dawla ruled it in the 980s, Diya' al-Dawla Basra), the Hasanwayhid and Kurdish chiefs' land and the Hamdanid Jazira front shifted in the 11th century, the Samanid frontier in Khorasan, the Byzantine front (a ten-year peace in 982), and who took Shiraz in 1062. Branch rulers: Jibal (Ray; Hamadan and Isfahan branches): Rukn al-Dawla 935-976, Fakhr al-Dawla 976-980, Mu'ayyad al-Dawla 980-983, Fakhr al-Dawla restored 984-997, Majd al-Dawla 997-1029; Hamadan: Mu'ayyad al-Dawla 976-983, Shams al-Dawla 997-1021, Sama' al-Dawla 1021-1024 (1021-1023 on the Majd page). Iraq: Mu'izz al-Dawla 945-967, 'Izz al-Dawla 966-978, 'Adud al-Dawla 978-983, Samsam al-Dawla 983-987, Sharaf al-Dawla 987-989, Baha' al-Dawla 989-1012, Sultan al-Dawla 1012-1021, Musharrif al-Dawla 1021-1025, Jalal al-Dawla 1025-1044, Abu Kalijar 1044-1048, Al-Malik al-Rahim 1048-1055. States needing dossiers: Uqaylids (Mosul, 989-), Kakuyids (Isfahan, from 1003 or 1023), Banu Ilyas (Kerman), Saffarids of Sistan (Khalaf ibn Ahmad), Hasanwayhids. Gazetteer: the Jibal has no region entry ('Jibal' / 'Iraq Ajami'); unions of Hamadan, Esfahan and a 150 km radius around Rey stand in for it.
